title: Goldblatt Trim Puller, Tile Removal Multi-Tool for Commercial Work & Home Improvement, Baseboard, Molding, Siding and Floor Removal, Remodeling

reviews.title: Internet videos made me buy this!
reviews.body: I needed to replace some baseboards in my house, and after seeing this tool on a video streaming platform, I knew I wanted it even though I probably could have made due for the small amount I was replacing.I am happy to say this worked an absolute treat! My baseboards were held on by glue, and this made taking them off a breeze with minimal damage to the drywall. Id imagine it would be equally as easy or even easier for nailed in baseboards since you can go in between them. I opted to replace them with slightly higher baseboards to hide any potential damage, but in hindsight that was probably not necessary!The tool itself feels solid and really good quality. There were others I saw selling for double or even triple the price, and I'm glad I opted for this one. I cant say for sure whether it would hold up over lots of use, but I didn't see any real signs of wear from the 1 room of baseboards I did and bet it would work great for anyone using it for non commercial purposes.10/ 10 would recommend, using this trim puller is oh so satisfying and makes the job a breeze!Read moreRead less

reviews.title: Helped me remove baseboards and window/door casing without damaging plaster!
reviews.body: Excellent tool!  I didn't even know this tool existed.  I had a bunch of baseboards to remove that was attached to old (1947) crumbly lathe and plaster so I needed a way to gently remove the baseboards without damaging the plaster.  Once you score the caulk line (if it exists) to separate the baseboard from the paint gently tapping this tools thin edge gets behind the baseboard and starts **gently** extracting the nails.  The further you can insert the tool behind the baseboard (or window/door trim) adds more fulcrum power and distributes the pushing power very gently.I had some boards that were original and the installer used REAL, thick nails.  They weren't going anywhere.  I took more time with these and let the tool do the work.  If you have such a scenario don't **man-handle** and force it out using brawn.  Let the tool use it fulcrum power, be patient and you wont damage the plaster.Oh, to be clear, it works very well on casing and window trim as well.  Great tool for the price.Highly recommended!Read moreRead less

reviews.title: Great For Removing Skirting Boards
reviews.body: Amazing product for removal of skirting boards in our house. Was initially using a hammer and chisel but this tool is making much lighter work of it.Very strong product and easy to use. Light enough to work for hours. Absolute steal at the price I purchased at and has saved me hours of work. Simply a case of wedging it into the skirting, give it a few knocks and start to pry off the wall.Read moreRead less

features: Trim Saving - The trim removal tool has a larger, flatter and wider contact area than clumsy traditional tools and features an integrated wedged center that provides increased removal efficiency and prevents damage to both the trim and wall.

Sturdy Pry Bars - Our trim puller is made from carbon steel and 65Mn steel with black electrophoretic and polished finish, which protects against corrosion and gives our pry bar added durability and strength. So the Trim Puller is a very beefy tool, and it will hold up well to repeated whacking.

Multi-Function - Ideal for commercial work, repair and remodel projects where care and precision are needed, including cabinets, countertops, flooring, and many more. It can be used on a kitchen remodel, removing a couple of sections of baseboard, a countertop from some base cabinets, and pulling up a ceramic tile floor. The very edge can also be used to pry up the staples.
Ergonomic Handle - All our trim puller is built with an ergonomic, comfortable and textured dipped handle. An impact-absorbing TPR+PP handle makes it comfortable to hold, though.

Revolutionary Tool - Our Trim Puller is a very beefy tool. The Built-in spring design assists in separating the trim from the wall freely and quickly. The 15-degree wedged center is for easy extraction of trim and baseboards.Goldblatt holds a U.S. patent for this Trim Puller, patent number US 11,142,921.
